name: Wild
tagline: Foraging intelligence — field to table, grounded in microclimate and accumulated observation.
description: Agent-led foraging and wild harvesting intelligence. Combines iNaturalist observation data, MycoBank nomenclature, microclimate forecasting, and a compounding personal knowledge graph to build the foraging expertise of a lifetime into a single creature. Rabble creatures consume Wild via cross-workspace delegation — the creature provides spatial context; Wild provides foraging intelligence.

schema_json.description: Action grammar for the Wild companion agent. Structures the foraging intelligence loop: scout location → assess conditions → identify species → evaluate harvest → log observation → update forecast.

canonical_document.description: The running observation log — species found, locations, conditions, dates, harvest notes, flavor assessments.

action_types.description: Ask what a photograph appears to show. Returns a determination labelled as the judgement it is, a taxonomy block resolved against GBIF and MycoBank, and a safety block that is permanently null with a platform-authored directive explaining why. Does NOT answer whether anything is safe to eat: the best of three popular phone identification apps was correct for 49% of 78 expert-confirmed specimens sent to a poisons centre, and death caps were misidentified by two of the three (Hodgson et al., Clin Toxicol 2023, PMID 36794335). Refusal is the product.

photo_url.description: Raw URL of an already-uploaded photograph

locality.description: Free-text locality. Deliberately not a coordinate — a precise location for a rare or over-collected species is a conservation risk.

habitat.description: Substrate and surroundings, as the submitter describes them

creature_context.description: A Rabble creature that was present. Context, not ownership: the corpus is App-scoped so determinations accumulate across every submitter.

action_types.description: Record a foraging observation. Creates a SOSA-compatible observation record, stores as an episode for KG accumulation via dream cycles.

species.description: Scientific or common name of what was found

h3_cell.description: H3 cell index of the find location

habitat.description: Substrate and habitat type e.g. 'oak woodland, leaf litter'

conditions.description: Observed microclimate: temp_c, humidity_pct, rainfall_prior_7d_mm, soil_moisture

harvest_notes.description: Notes on harvest quality, maturity, damage

flavor_notes.description: Tasting notes if consumed: aroma, texture, taste dimensions

opted_in_shared.description: Contribute this observation to the shared regional model

action_types.description: Record progress against a creature's standing foraging goal. Updates the goal's progress JSONB and fires a push notification if the goal condition is met.

progress_delta.description: What changed: { new_species, locations_visited, observations_logged, notable_event }

goal_achieved.description: True if the goal condition has been fully met

notable_event.description: Human-readable description of the notable find e.g. 'First Cantharellus cibarius at this location'

action_types.description: Record a named foraging location with habitat characteristics. Persists to wild/locations.yaml. Accumulates into the creature's KG as a location entity.

seasonal_notes.description: When this spot is productive and under what conditions

# Wild Foraging Journal

This workspace accumulates your foraging intelligence over time.

## How it works

1. **Scout** — ask wild_companion what's likely fruiting near your location
2. **Log** — record what you actually find via log_observation
3. **Dream** — trigger your creature's dream cycle to distill patterns
4. **Learn** — future scouts draw on your accumulated knowledge

## Data sources
- iNaturalist: community observations near your location
- MycoBank: authoritative fungal nomenclature
- GBIF: species distribution and taxonomy
- Openweather: microclimate conditions for fruiting forecasts
- Your own observations: the most valuable signal

## Privacy
All observations are private by default. Opt in to `opted_in_shared: true`
to contribute to the shared regional model and receive better predictions.
